topic: Template Function Specialization and SFINAE for Conditional Function Overloading
explanation: In C++, templates enable generic programming by allowing functions and classes to operate with generic types. Template specialization and SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) are advanced techniques that control template instantiation, enabling conditional compilation of template functions based on type traits or other compile-time conditions. These features are essential for writing flexible, type-safe, and efficient code that adapts to different types or conditions without runtime overhead.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates how SFINAE and std::enable_if are used to conditionally enable different template function overloads based on the type traits of the argument. When an integer is passed, the integral version is instantiated; when a floating-point value is passed, the floating-point version is instantiated. This technique allows for compile-time function selection, enhancing code flexibility and type safety in modern C++ programming.
